find_problems.summary: Breathlessness with a raised BNP in a patient with type 2 diabetes.

prompts.text:
You are reading a consult draft to list the clinical problems it names.

Task:
List each distinct problem the draft names — a diagnosis, a finding still to be explained, or a decision still to be made — once, in the order the draft first raises it. For each, give its name and one or two sentences of what the draft says about it: its findings, and the plan the draft records for it. Then write a one-sentence summary of the consultation.

Guardrail:
Use only what the draft contains. Do not add problems, findings or plans it does not name. Group what belongs to one problem under that problem rather than listing it twice.

Consult draft:
Priya Raman, 67, seen for breathlessness. Known type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 61 mmol/mol on metformin. New ankle swelling; BNP raised, echo requested. Review in clinic in four weeks with the echo result. (Fictional.)

Answer with one JSON object conforming to this schema.
{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"required":["summary","problems"],"properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"},"problems":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"required":["name","detail"],"properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"detail":{"type":"string"}}}}}}

You are deciding one thing about a consult draft: whether it arranges for the patient to be reassessed.

Definitions:
Yes: the draft schedules a further visit, review or reassessment with this clinic — at a stated time or interval.
No: the draft arranges no further visit with this clinic, or says only that the patient may be seen again if needed.

Guardrail:
Decide from the draft alone. A referral to another service, a test to be done, or a medication to start is not a reassessment by itself.

Consult draft:
Priya Raman, 67, seen for breathlessness. Known type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 61 mmol/mol on metformin. New ankle swelling; BNP raised, echo requested. Review in clinic in four weeks with the echo result. (Fictional.)
